name: Orkes: LLM Task Fails Because llmProvider Is a Provider Type, Not an Integration Name
query: My summarize_ticket workflow works on my local Conductor but on our Orkes cluster the LLM_CHAT_COMPLETE task fails saying the integration 'anthropic' was not found. The task has llmProvider: "anthropic" and model: "claude-sonnet-4-6". Our admins say Anthropic is configured. What's wrong and how do I fix it?
expected_behavior: Step 1: Explain that on Orkes `llmProvider` is the name of an integration configured on the cluster, not the provider type — locally (OSS) `anthropic` is the provider name, so the same JSON works there
Step 2: List the cluster's AI integrations: `python3 "$CONDUCTOR_API" integration-list --category AI_MODEL` to find the actual Anthropic integration name
Step 3: Check the model is registered under it: `python3 "$CONDUCTOR_API" model-list --provider <name>`; if `claude-sonnet-4-6` is missing, register it with `model-save` (or ask the admins to)
Step 4: Check the application running the workflow has access to the integration (`access-list --target-id <name>`), and grant it if needed
Step 5: Update `llmProvider` to the integration name, write the workflow to a file, `conductor workflow update`, and re-run to verify
success_criteria: Identifies the cause: on Orkes `llmProvider` must be the integration NAME configured on the cluster, which differs from the provider type that works on OSS
Lists the cluster's AI integrations (`integration-list` or `GET /api/integrations/provider`) to find the real name rather than guessing
Checks that the model is registered under that integration (`model-list` / `model-save`)
Mentions checking or granting the running application's access to the integration
Fixes the workflow by changing `llmProvider` to the integration name, writing the JSON to a file and updating/re-running it
Does not suggest replacing the task with an HTTP call to api.anthropic.com, and does not tell the user to set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY on the Orkes server as the fix
